briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for November 7, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 COP31 Imminent and the Challenges for the International Community
sections.content: The international climate conference, COP31, is set to begin on Monday [25], with institutions such as the University of Colorado Boulder preparing to attend [24]. Amid growing interest in what will be discussed at COP31 and its potential impact on South Korea's climate policy [1], reports indicate that the global scientific panel has encountered difficulties ahead of the COP31 climate summit [29]. There is a strong call for commitments to climate change to be accompanied by concrete actions [4]. Alongside expectations for what COP31 can achieve in energy transition [35], discussions are also underway on how COP climate summits can have a useful future [31]. However, concerns are also being raised about the limitations of international climate negotiations, including the failure to achieve the core temperature targets of the Paris Agreement and the exclusion of specific plans for national greenhouse gas emission reductions from the negotiation agenda [41].

sections.title: ⚠️ Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Impacts
sections.content: Warnings have emerged that global temperatures in October 2026 reached an 'all-time high,' making it certain that the 1.5°C threshold will be exceeded [6]. This climate change is exacerbating humanitarian crises worldwide, including food insecurity for children due to the war in Sudan [19] and making it more difficult for Turkish refugees to leave their homes [27, 34]. Direct impacts of the climate crisis are widely observed, such as the spread of dengue fever to high-altitude Himalayan regions [22] and historic autumn heatwaves [26]. The world's largest penguin colony has lost 63% of its population, with scientists attributing this to climate change [40]. An editorial also suggested a link between climate change and antibiotic resistance in animal health [30]. The outgoing UN Secretary-General characterized the fight to curb global warming as a 'moment of truth' [39], and Arctic scientists urged world leaders to take urgent action on climate change [32].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Renewable Energy Expansion
sections.content: Domestically, efforts by businesses and local communities for carbon neutrality are active. Woori Financial Group Chairman Lim Jong-ryong met with the head of MSCI to discuss climate change and AI responses [2, 3], and Yeosu Gwangyang Port Authority received recognition for its ESG performance by winning the Sustainable Management Quality Grand Prize [12]. Korea Western Power Seoincheon Power Plant won the Ministerial Award for Carbon Neutrality and Green Management [8], Gyeongsang National University is comprehensively expanding carbon neutrality education [7], and local communities, such as Goryeong-gun and Ulsan Dong-gu Saemaul Association, are holding carbon neutrality pledge ceremonies [9, 10]. Expectations are particularly high for the expansion of renewable energy supply, with Bonghwa-gun being selected for the 'Carbon Neutral' Agriculture and Rural RE100 demonstration project [11], and Korea East-West Power promoting local economic revitalization in Goyang through solar power projects [13]. Chairman Nam Jong-seop stated his commitment to supporting resident-participatory renewable energy projects [14], and institutional support for the spread of resident-participatory renewable energy [15] is also being strengthened, with the government discussing preferential treatment for agrivoltaics power generation profits and preparing countermeasures for the revision of the RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) [16].

sections.title: 🌱 New Initiatives and Strategies for Climate Change Response
sections.content: Various new initiatives and strategies for responding to climate change are being explored both domestically and internationally. The N.W.T. government has announced a new energy and climate change strategy [37], and the 'blue wave' in the midterm elections is expected to act as a check on President Trump, positively impacting renewable energy [33]. In the Marlborough region, the link between wild fermentation and climate change was discussed [28], and efforts to raise public awareness of climate issues continue, such as addressing the relationship between sand mining and climate change in the 'Climate Action Opportunity Income Quiz' [5]. Furthermore, reports that the 'Climate Change Game Jam' is not about the game itself [38] suggest the importance of diverse participation and creative approaches from various fields to solve climate change issues. Meanwhile, news of the commencement of construction for the 180MW Ban Khan 2 wind power plant, classified as [domestic] [17], demonstrates ongoing international efforts to expand renewable energy.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again underscores the severity of the climate crisis, the urgent need for responsible action from the international community to address it, and the critical importance of diverse efforts both domestically and internationally. This concludes today's climate briefing.
